acceptance: The upgrade mirror holds tracked files, untracked non-ignored files and what the refreshes read, so gitignored paths such as .env files, virtualenvs, node_modules and nested repos are never copied to the temp directory, on a real run or a dry run
A dry run builds the mirror once or reuses it, prints a line before copying, and its plan matches the real run as today

tests prove an ignored secret file and an ignored directory are absent from the mirror on both paths, and that a plan on a checkout with large ignored content equals the plan without it; docs and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry
nodes.title: upgrade mirrors only what the refreshes need, never ignored files

pyproject.toml has Project-URL entries, README links that readers need from the package are absolute, and the RC guide says moving to a newer RC is a fresh install of the new URL because uv tool upgrade stays on a URL pin
project.version is not changed; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry
nodes.title: Each RC publishes its wheel URL and install line, and the package links to the guide

acceptance: On a machine where the Cursor sandbox starts, the documented default launch (sandbox on, no --force) runs a worker and a reviewer turn, and the result is recorded
The run records whether the CLI reports its model and whether it matches the request, how --resume with a new prompt behaves, and whether --mode ask suits reviewers
docs/orchestration-workers.md states what was confirmed; findings about the Cursor IDE stay separate from CLI findings
nodes.title: Test the Cursor CLI harness on the documented default

acceptance: doctor --fix leaves a registry row with no branch in this clone or on the remote, reports it as advisory with what to check, and still removes a row whose leaf is Complete
Removing a no-branch row takes the existing explicit registry-prune path, named in the report
tests/test_doctor.py covers both rows through the CLI; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry
nodes.title: doctor --fix never removes a claim that may belong to another clone

acceptance: sweep_stalled also flags a running worker that never produced output, measured from its launch, and worker sync, worker list and doctor all show stalled workers with how long they have been silent

specy-road worker recover ends a stalled worker, keeps its worktree and commits, and resumes the native session with the continue prompt, or says why it cannot; it runs once and exits: no daemon, no background loop

Recovery is bounded: a retry limit per worker from policy, one recovery at a time per leaf, never a second live worker on a leaf, and a worker past the limit stops as needing a person with its last output named
grind-session calls the same recovery on its own loop; a stalled worker no longer waits for a person to notice

tests/test_worker_stall_recovery.py covers silent output, no output at all, a recovered worker, the retry limit and a leaf with a live worker; docs/orchestration-workers.md describes it; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry
nodes.title: Stalled workers are detected on every run and can be recovered in one command

tests/test_model_names.py covers Opus, Sol and Grok names in both context sizes, and a mismatch that must stay a mismatch; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry
